attack_classes.mapping: A yanked or patched Log4j release did not move clients whose lockfile/cache still held 2.14.1. execute_cached is a public execute path and still calls verify_package, which fail-closes on a stale CRL and on a revoked id.

claims.scoped_restatement: The index may be the control plane for what is listed. Execution still requires verify_package; without it, index-as-control-plane is a fail-open loader.

claims.claim: A lockfile-pinned package is supply-chain safe, so already-installed content may run without re-verification.
claims.scoped_restatement: A lockfile pins id and version. Safety against signature-stripped or revoked-but-cached bytes requires the MAC and CRL steps on execute_cached as well as install.
claims.why_locus: lockfile-pinned is a catalogue phrase. DESIGN.json for [REDACTED] is absent, so there is no [REDACTED] rule to refute; the overclaim is the sentence that pinning implies byte safety.

legacy_root.question: Threat-model the marketplace as an attack surface: malicious or over-permissioned package, typosquatted id, unsigned or signature-stripped artifact, dependency confusion between a private mirror and a public one, and a revocation that never reaches an already-installed client. Specify the MANDATORY verification a client performs before executing ANY package content, and prove no install path skips it.

scenario.catching_architecture: [REDACTED] [REDACTED] with mandatory verify_package before execute_package_content on every public lifecycle path in command-center/p2-wave/probes/[REDACTED]/client.py, including execute_cached.
procedure: Build a lockfile pinning skill.hello@1.0.0 from owner-private-index.
Build a package with valid id/version/source/permissions and an HMAC over those bytes.
Strip or zero the signature field while leaving metadata intact.
Offer the stripped package to every PUBLIC_EXECUTE_PATHS entry, including execute_cached.
Assert each path returns executed=False with reason signature-verification-failed.
scenario.title: Metadata-valid signature-stripped package must not execute

legacy_root.strongest_surviving_counterargument: Under PR-ONLY the owner is the only publisher, so HMAC-SHA256 with the owner key is the smallest binding that still fails closed on stripped bytes. A second publisher would make this MAC insufficient (no per-publisher keys). That is dead-weight under the single-owner cost model, not a reason to skip the choke. The index can remain the control plane for what is listed; it is not a substitute for verify-before-execute. Do not rebuild [REDACTED] DESIGN.json in this unit (no ADV circle). Generated [REDACTED] marketplace_entry JSON is metadata-only and is not an execute path.
